issues.description: The template's addGuestStudents method signature does not match the specification and the solution. The problem statement and UML expect addGuestStudents(int) (single int parameter), and the reference solution implements addGuestStudents(int). The template, however, declares addGuestStudents(int, boolean), which will confuse students and prevent them from following the specified API or matching the solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java and remove the extra boolean parameter (or provide an overloaded single-parameter version). Update the method body comment/implementation accordingly so students implement the intended API.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution implement addGuestStudents(int): void (single int parameter). The template's Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (an extra boolean parameter and different signature). This signature mismatch across artifacts can confuse students about which method to implement and how the method should be used.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... }. If input validation is desired, implement it internally (e.g., validate inside the method) or document the additional parameter in the problem statement so all artifacts agree.
